### Autoimmunity

```{r summarize_autoimmunity_old, include=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
autoimmune_summary <- gen_health_nested %>%
  unnest(c(condition_BL, Other_autoimmune_BL, Type_1_or_2_BL), keep_empty = T) %>%
  count(condition_BL, vit_status_exp) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  mutate(prop = n/sum(n), .by = condition_BL)

# establish the order of conditions to appear by Highest % of vitiligo-affected
condition_order <- autoimmune_summary %>%
  # filter for vit pt's
  filter(vit_status_exp == "vitiligo") %>%
  arrange(desc(prop)) %>%
  mutate(prop_fac = factor(prop))


# condense autoimmune summary
autoimmune_thresholds <- autoimmune_summary %>% 
  summarize(tot_responses = sum(n), .by = condition_BL) %>% 
  arrange(desc(tot_responses)) %>% 
  mutate(threshold = tot_responses/sum(tot_responses))

autoimmune_conditions_prevalent <- autoimmune_thresholds %>%
  filter(threshold >= 0.03) %>%
```

```{r extract_other_autoimmune_conds, include=FALSE}
# unnest relevant autoimmune response cols
autoimmune_unnested <- gen_health_nested %>%
  unnest(c(condition_BL, Other_autoimmune_BL, Type_1_or_2_BL), keep_empty = T) %>%
  # remove excess space from free text responses
  mutate(Other_autoimmune_BL = case_when(condition_BL == "other" ~ str_squish(Other_autoimmune_BL)))


# refactor "Other" conditions
autoimmune_other_conds <- autoimmune_unnested %>%
  mutate(
    # remove "other" conditions for records where condition is a given choice
    # any response with these characters gets re-classified as "other"
    Other_autoimmune_BL = case_when(str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "didn.?t fit all the criteria|diagnos") ~ "other",
                                    .default = Other_autoimmune_BL),
    # split "other" col on ", | with | and"
    Other_autoimmune_BL = str_split(Other_autoimmune_BL, ", | with | and ")
  ) %>%
  # create new rows with each split of "Other" col
  unnest(Other_autoimmune_BL) %>%
  mutate(
    other_conditions_fac = case_when(
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "diabet.{2}") ~ "diabetes",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "lichen") ~ "LS",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "r(ay |ey)naud") ~ "raynauds",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "urticaria") ~ "urticaria",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "chronic") ~ str_replace(Other_autoimmune_BL, "chronic", ""),
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "granuloma") ~ "granuloma annulare",
      # str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "didn.?t fit all the criteria|not been diagnosed") ~ "other",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "diverticulitis") ~ "diverticulitis",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "high blood pressure") ~ "hbp",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "h.+nitis s.+tiva") ~ "HS",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "hypermobil") ~ "hypermobility",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "hypo.*thyroid") ~ "hypothyroidism",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "gluten|dairy") ~ "glu_dairy_free",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "i.+cystitis") ~ "IC",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "arthritis|rheumat") ~ "arthritis",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "low.*thyroid") ~ "hypothyroidism",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "pandas|pans") ~ "pandas_pans",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "small fiber neuropathy") ~ "SFN",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "sjogren") ~ "sjogrens",
      str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "anemi(c|a)") ~ "anemia",
      .default = Other_autoimmune_BL
    ),
    other_conditions_fac = str_squish(other_conditions_fac),
    # set condition as "other" condition UNLESS its diabetes --> breakdown diabetes even further
    condition_BL = case_when((condition_BL == "diabetes" | other_conditions_fac == "diabetes") & Type_1_or_2_BL == "type 1" ~ "diabetes_1", 
                             (condition_BL == "diabetes" | other_conditions_fac == "diabetes") & Type_1_or_2_BL == "type 2" ~ "diabetes_2",
                             (condition_BL == "diabetes" | other_conditions_fac == "diabetes") & str_detect(Other_autoimmune_BL, "gestational.+diabet") ~ "diabetes_gest",
                             (condition_BL == "diabetes" | other_conditions_fac == "diabetes") & Type_1_or_2_BL %in% c("i don't know", NA) ~ "diabetes_na",
                             condition_BL == "other" & !is.na(other_conditions_fac) ~ other_conditions_fac,
                             .default = condition_BL),
    # factorize and assign NA label to these levels
    condition_BL = factor(condition_BL) %>% fct_na_level_to_value(extra_levels = c("no", "i don't know"))
  ) %>%
  select(
    patient_id:Other_autoimmune_BL,
    other_conditions_fac,
    everything()
  )
```

```{r summarize_prevalent_autoimmune_conds, include=FALSE}
# compute the "threshold" of each reported condition (% of total responses)

# autoimmune_thresholds <- autoimmune_other_conds %>%
#   # remove responses which report having "vitiligo" as "other" autoimmune cond
#   filter(
#     is.na(condition_BL) | str_detect(condition_BL, str_to_lower("vitiligo"), negate = T)
#   ) %>%
#   count(condition_BL) %>%
#   rename(tot_resp = n) %>%
#   mutate(prop_resp = tot_resp / sum(tot_resp)) %>%
#   arrange(desc(tot_resp)) %>%
#   # filter out any diabetes that is NOT type 1 (only type 1 is autoimmune)
#   filter(!condition_BL %in% str_c("diabetes", c("2", "na", "gest"), sep = "_"))

autoimmune_thresholds <- autoimmune_other_conds %>%
  # remove responses which report having "vitiligo" as "other" autoimmune cond
  filter(
    is.na(condition_BL) | str_detect(condition_BL, str_to_lower("vitiligo"), negate = T)
  ) %>%
  group_by(condition_BL) %>%
  summarize(pt_with_cond = n_distinct(patient_id)) %>%
  mutate(total_pt = n_distinct(autoimmune_other_conds$patient_id)) %>%
  mutate(incidence_rate = pt_with_cond / total_pt) %>%
  arrange(desc(incidence_rate)) %>%
  # filter out any diabetes that is NOT type 1 (only type 1 is autoimmune)
  filter(!condition_BL %in% str_c("diabetes", c("2", "na", "gest"), sep = "_"))

# subset only the conditions reported by 2% or more of total cohort
autoimmune_conditions_prevalent_df <- autoimmune_thresholds %>% 
  # filter(prop_resp >= 0.025)
  filter(incidence_rate >= 0.02)

# TODO: summarize counts & props of autoimmune conditions x vit status; filter for prevalent conditions; convert the rest to "other"
autoimmune_condensed <- autoimmune_other_conds %>%
  mutate(
    # keep 'prevalent' conditions and convert the rest to "other"
    condition_condensed = fct_other(condition_BL, 
                                    keep = as.character(autoimmune_conditions_prevalent_df$condition_BL), 
                                    other_level = "other") %>% fct_na_value_to_level(level = "no condition")
  ) %>%
  # filter out "vitiligo" and any diabetes condition that is NOT type 1
  filter(
    # filter for responses where condensed is not "other" OR it is "other" and not...
    condition_condensed != "other" |
      (condition_condensed == "other" & !condition_BL %in% c("vitiligo", str_c("diabetes", c("2", "na", "gest"), sep = "_")))
    # !condition_BL %in% str_c("diabetes", c("2", "na", "gest"), sep = "_")
  ) %>%
  select(patient_id:vit_status_exp, condition_condensed, everything())


autoimmune_condensed_summary <- autoimmune_condensed %>%
  count(condition_condensed, vit_status_exp) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  mutate(prop = n/sum(n), .by = condition_condensed)
```

```{r}
# init. counts of participants who are affected vs unaffected with vitiligo
vit_counts_under30 <- autoimmune_condensed %>%
  # add ages
  inner_join(y = patients_clean_age %>% select(patient_id, age_yr_end),
             by = "patient_id") %>%
  # categorize whether someone is 30+ or under
  mutate(under_30yo = age_yr_end <= 29) %>%
  # only 1 record per participant
  distinct(patient_id, recorded_date, .keep_all = T) %>%
  count(vit_status_exp, under_30yo) %>%
  # if there are any NAs for under_30yo --> convert them to F
  mutate(under_30yo = if_else(is.na(under_30yo),
                              F,
                              under_30yo)) %>%
  mutate(n = sum(n), .by = c(vit_status_exp, under_30yo)) %>% distinct(vit_status_exp, under_30yo, .keep_all = T)


# Summary Table that adds an age covariate --> whether or not someone is 30 years old or order
autoimmune_condensed_summary_v3 <- autoimmune_condensed %>%
  # add ages
  inner_join(
    y = patients_clean_age %>% select(patient_id, age_yr_end),
    by = "patient_id"
  ) %>%
  # categorize whether someone is 30+ or under
  mutate(under_30yo = if_else(is.na(age_yr_end), F, age_yr_end <= 29)) %>%
  summarize(
    cases = n_distinct(patient_id),
    .by = c(vit_status_exp, under_30yo, condition_condensed)
  ) %>%
  # compute total number of pts who are healthy/vitiligo and under/over 30
  mutate(
    total_patients = case_when(
      vit_status_exp == "healthy" & under_30yo ~ vit_counts_under30 %>% filter(vit_status_exp == "healthy", under_30yo) %>% pull(n),
      vit_status_exp == "healthy" & !under_30yo ~ vit_counts_under30 %>% filter(vit_status_exp == "healthy", !under_30yo) %>% pull(n),
      vit_status_exp == "vitiligo" & under_30yo ~ vit_counts_under30 %>% filter(vit_status_exp == "vitiligo", under_30yo) %>% pull(n),
      vit_status_exp == "vitiligo" & !under_30yo ~ vit_counts_under30 %>% filter(vit_status_exp == "vitiligo", !under_30yo) %>% pull(n)
    )
  ) %>%
  # compute prevalence rate for a given condition
  mutate(prevalence_rate = cases / total_patients)
```

```{r autoimmunity_chi_sq, echo=FALSE}
# compute chi-square test

# create contingency table
autoimmune_condensed_table <- table(
  autoimmune_condensed$vit_status_exp, 
  autoimmune_condensed$condition_condensed
)

(autoimmune_chisq <- chisq.test(autoimmune_condensed_table))
```

The results of this chi-square test suggest that there is a __statistically significant__ association between having vitiligo and reporting another autoimmune condition.

```{r print_autoimmune_incidence_ratios_og, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# compute incidence ratios for each prevalent autoimmune disease
autoimmune_condensed_table %>%
  as.data.frame.matrix() %>%
  # rownames_to_column() %>%
  # as_tibble %>%
  mutate(across(.cols = where(is.integer),
                .fns = ~ .x / sum(.x))) %>%
  mutate(
    across(.cols = where(is.numeric),
           .fns = ~ case_when(.x == min(.x) ~ 1,
                              .default = round((.x / (sum(.x) - .x)) / 0.25) * 0.25))
  ) %>%
  print.data.frame()
```

```{r print_autoimmune_incidence_ratios, echo=FALSE}
### TEST ###

autoimmune_condensed %>%
  # Count cases for each condition in vitiligo and healthy groups
  group_by(vit_status_exp, condition_condensed) %>%
  summarize(cases = n_distinct(patient_id), .groups = "drop") %>%
  
  # Calculate total patients in vitiligo and healthy groups
  group_by(vit_status_exp) %>%
  mutate(total_patients = n_distinct(autoimmune_condensed$patient_id[autoimmune_condensed$vit_status_exp == first(vit_status_exp)])) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  
  # Calculate incidence rates
  mutate(incidence_rate = cases / total_patients) %>%
  
  # Pivot to wide format to get vitiligo and healthy rates side by side
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = condition_condensed,
    names_from = vit_status_exp,
    values_from = c(cases, total_patients, incidence_rate),
    names_glue = "{vit_status_exp}_{.value}"
  ) %>%
  
  # Calculate incidence ratios for both vitiligo and healthy
  mutate(
    vitiligo_ratio = vitiligo_incidence_rate / healthy_incidence_rate,
    healthy_ratio = healthy_incidence_rate / vitiligo_incidence_rate
  ) %>%
  
  # Select only the columns we need
  select(condition_condensed, vitiligo_ratio, healthy_ratio) %>%
  
  # Sort by vitiligo ratio in descending order
  arrange(desc(vitiligo_ratio)) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(across(.cols = c(vitiligo_ratio, healthy_ratio),
                .fns = ~ case_when(.x < 1 ~ 1,
                                   .default = round(.x * 2, 0) / 2))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  as.data.frame.data.frame() %>%
  column_to_rownames("condition_condensed") %>% 
  t() %>%
  print.table()
```



<!-- Now testing vitiligo status * plex status... -->


<!-- Approx. incidence ratios for each autoimmune condition: -->

```{r print_autoimmune_vit_x_plex_incidence_ratios, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# view autoimmunity through lens of plex
autoimmune_condensed_plex <- autoimmune_condensed %>%
  left_join(
    y = patients_clean,
    by = "patient_id",
    suffix = c("", "_pt")
  ) %>%
  select(any_of(colnames(autoimmune_condensed)), plex) %>%
  select(patient_id, plex, everything()) %>%
  # combine plex + vit_status_exp to create 1 independent variable
  unite(vit_status_exp, plex, col = "IV", sep = "_")

# glm(
#   condition_condensed ~ vit_status_exp * plex,
#   family = binomial,
#   data = autoimmune_condensed_plex
# ) %>% summary()

autoimmune_condensed_plex_table <- table(
  autoimmune_condensed_plex$IV,
  autoimmune_condensed_plex$condition_condensed
)


# compute incidence ratios for each prevalent autoimmune disease
autoimmune_condensed_plex_table %>%
  as.data.frame.matrix() %>%
  rownames_to_column() %>%
  as_tibble %>% 
  arrange(rowname) %>%
  mutate(across(.cols = where(is.integer),
                .fns = ~ .x / sum(.x))) %>%
                # .fns = ~ round((.x / (sum(.x) - .x)) / 0.5) * 0.5)) %>%
  mutate(across(.cols = where(is.numeric),
                .fns = ~ case_when(.x == 0 ~ NA, .default = .x))) %>%
  mutate(
    aa_scale = 1 / min(`alopecia areata`, na.rm = T),
    ht_scale = 1 / min(`hashimoto thyroiditis`, na.rm = T),
    p_scale = 1 / min(psoriasis, na.rm = T),
    o_scale = 1 / min(other, na.rm = T),
    nc_scale = 1 / min(`no condition`, na.rm = T)
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    alopecia_areata_ratio = prod(`alopecia areata`, aa_scale, na.rm = F),
    hashimoto_thyroiditis_ratio = prod(`hashimoto thyroiditis`, ht_scale, na.rm = F),
    psoriasis_ratio = prod(psoriasis, p_scale, na.rm = F), 
    other_ratio = prod(other, o_scale, na.rm = F),
    no_condition_ratio = prod(`no condition`, nc_scale, na.rm = F)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(rowname, alopecia_areata_ratio:no_condition_ratio) %>%
  mutate(across(.cols = where(is.numeric),
                .fns = ~ round(.x / 0.25) * 0.25)) %>%
                # .fns = ~round(.x))) %>%
  column_to_rownames() %>%
  print.data.frame()
```

Now lets evaluate the effect of family type (simplex vs multiplex) among JUST healthy people and JUST vitiligo people on autoimmunity. Here is the 2x2 contingency table:

```{r print_autoimmunebool_healthyplex_contingency_table, echo=FALSE}
  select(patient_id:IV, condition_bool, condition_condensed, everything()) %>%
  distinct(patient_id, recorded_date, .keep_all = T)

  filter(str_detect(IV, "healthy")) %>%
```

The plots do NOT suggest a significant association between healthy-vitiligo or simplex-multiplex & melanoma diagnosis.


Chi-square test to evaluate the significance of a person's vitiligo status (healthy vs. vitiligo) on their melanoma diagnosis:

```{r melanoma_x_vit_chisq, echo=FALSE}
# chi-square to evaluate melanoma ~ vit_status * plex
```

Chi-square test to evaluate the significance of a person's 'family type' (simplex vs multiplex) on their melanoma diagnosis:

```{r melanoma_x_plex_chisq, echo=FALSE}
melanoma_plex_table <- table(
  melanoma_unnested$plex,
  melanoma_unnested$melanoma_BL
)

chisq.test(melanoma_plex_table)
```

What if we combine these 2 independent variables into 1 with four levels: "healthy_simplex", "healthy_multiplex", "vitiligo_simplex", "vitiligo_multilpex"


```{r melanoma_iv_chisq, echo=FALSE}
melanoma_iv <- melanoma_unnested %>%

melanoma_iv_table <- table(
  melanoma_iv$IV,
  melanoma_iv$melanoma_BL
)

chisq.test(melanoma_iv_table)
```

Among just cancer-diagnosed individuals, having vitiligo and/or belonging to a multiplex family appears to have __no significant effect__ on melanoma diagnosis.

```{r}
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(patient_id:plex),
    names_to = "original_field",
    values_to = "response"
  ) %>% 
  # filter(str_detect(patient_id, "92_2"), str_detect(original_field, "(V|v)itiligo_(D|d)iagnosis"))
  # join standard names on current DF
  left_join(
    y = vit_mapping_df,
    by = c("original_field" = "bl_fields"),
    suffix = c("", "_map1")
  ) %>%
  # if any standard fields are NA, replace them with the original field value
  # mutate(standard_name = if_else(is.na(standard_name), original_field, standard_name)) %>%
  left_join(
    y = vit_mapping_df,
    by = c("original_field" = "qt_fields"),
    suffix = c("", "_map2")
  ) %>%
  # combine both standard_name fields to remove NAs at each index
  mutate(standard_name = coalesce(standard_name, standard_name_map2)) %>% 
  filter(str_detect(original_field, survey_type)) %>%
  select(-c(original_field, qt_fields, bl_fields, standard_name_map2)) %>%
  relocate(response, .after = ncol(.))
```



```{r}
vit_survey_unnested <- vit_survey_standard %>%
  unnest(cols = response)


vit_survey_test_1 <- vit_survey_unnested %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = standard_name,
              values_from = response,
              values_fn = list) %>%
  unnest(cols = vit_diagnosis, keep_empty = T) %>%
  filter(n() > 1, .by = patient_id) %>%
  arrange(patient_id, recorded_date) %>%
  left_join(y = survey_cycle_summary %>% select(patient_id, enroll_day) %>% distinct(patient_id, .keep_all = T), by = "patient_id", suffix = c("", "_extra")) %>%
  relocate(enroll_day, .before = 2)

# deduplicate BL surveys (keep the earliest if duplicates exist)
vit_survey_test_1 %>%
  filter(if_else(survey_type == "BL", recorded_date == min(recorded_date), T),
         .by = c(patient_id, survey_type)) %>%
  # number QT surveys with each participant
  arrange(patient_id, recorded_date) %>%
  mutate(
    qt_number = if_else(survey_type == "QT", row_number() - sum(survey_type == "BL"), NA),
    survey_type = if_else(survey_type == "QT", str_c("QT", qt_number), survey_type),
    .by = patient_id
  ) %>%
  # reshape to wide format
  # select(patient_id, survey_type, vit_diagnosis) %>%
  filter(patient_id %in% c( "VIGOR_306_4_v", "VIGOR_325_5", "VIGOR_504_5", "VIGOR_504_6", "VIGOR_602_2"))
```

```{r}
# library(dplyr)
# library(tidyr)
# library(lubridate)

# Function to coalesce duplicates within a group
coalesce_duplicates <- function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) return(NA)  # If all responses are NA, return NA
  if (any(is.na(x))) return(coalesce(!!!x))  # If any NA exists, coalesce responses
  return(last(x))  # If no NA, return the latest response
}

# Step 1: Compute the quarter for each survey (independently for BL and QT)
vit_survey_clean <- vit_survey_test_1 %>%
  mutate(quarter = floor(interval(start = enroll_day, end = recorded_date) / months(3))) %>%
  arrange(patient_id, survey_type, recorded_date)

# Step 2: Identify the first survey in each quarter for each survey type
vit_survey_clean <- vit_survey_clean %>%
  group_by(patient_id, survey_type, quarter) %>%
  mutate(is_first_of_quarter = recorded_date == min(recorded_date)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Step 3: Resolve duplicate BL and QT surveys within the same quarter separately
vit_survey_dedup <- vit_survey_clean %>%
  group_by(patient_id, survey_type, quarter) %>%
  summarise(across(vit_diagnosis, coalesce_duplicates), 
            recorded_date = max(recorded_date),  # Keep latest response
            .groups = "drop") 

# Step 4: Assign QT numbers sequentially for each participant
vit_survey_dedup <- vit_survey_dedup %>%
  arrange(patient_id, survey_type, quarter) %>%
  group_by(patient_id) %>%
  mutate(qt_number = ifelse(survey_type == "QT", row_number(), NA),
         survey_type = ifelse(survey_type == "QT", paste0("QT", qt_number), survey_type)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Step 5: Reshape to wide format
vit_survey_wide <- vit_survey_dedup %>%
  select(patient_id, survey_type, vit_diagnosis) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = survey_type, values_from = vit_diagnosis, names_prefix = "vit_diagnosis_")

# View result
print(vit_survey_wide)
```

#### t-test/rank-sum


Statistical analyses to evaluate difference in age of onset b/w family type (simplex vs. multilpex)

```{r ttest_vit_age_onset, echo=FALSE}
# independent samples t-test
t.test(vitiligo_onset_BL ~ plex, data = vit_age_onset)

# vectors of ages of onset for each group
simplex_ages <- vit_age_onset %>% filter(plex == "simplex") %>% pull(vitiligo_onset_BL)
multiplex_ages <- vit_age_onset %>% filter(plex == "multiplex") %>% pull(vitiligo_onset_BL)
```

Check for normality in ages of onset among simplex participants:

```{r shapiro_simplex_vit_age_onset, echo=FALSE}
# check normality in simplex ages
shapiro.test(simplex_ages)
```

Check for normality in ages of onset among multiplex participants:

```{r shapiro_multiplex_vit_age_onset, echo=FALSE}
# check normality in multiplex ages
shapiro.test(multiplex_ages)
```

The low p-values of these two shapiro-wilk tests suggests that the ages of onset for simplex and multiplex participants are both non-normally distributed. We can also infer this from the histogram/density plots. 

Independent samples t-test does not meet the normality assumption since ages of onset are not distributed normally. Need to do Wilcoxon rank-sum test instead...


```{r wilcox_vit_age_onset, echo=FALSE}
wilcox.test(vitiligo_onset_BL ~ plex, data = vit_age_onset)
```

Given the p-value, we can conclude that there is __no significant difference__ in age of vitiligo onset between individuals in simplex vs. multiplex families.


#### Fit to Bimodal Distribution

Use a bimodal gaussian fit to categorize early-onset and late-onset groups within each family type.


However, we note that previous tests and visual inspection show that age of onset is distributed non-normally in both family types. 


```{r fit_bimodal_gmm_vit_age_onset, include=FALSE}
# fitting a mixture of bimodal normal distributions using Expectation-Maximization
gmm_fit <- normalmixEM(
  # vector of data to fit to
  x = vit_age_onset %>% filter(!is.na(vitiligo_onset_BL)) %>% pull(vitiligo_onset_BL),
  # number of 'normal components' (peaks) in the data
  k = 2
)
```


```{r plot_bimodal_gmm_vit_age_onset_test, include=FALSE}
# plot the fitted bimodal gaussian model over our density plot
vit_age_onset_densityplot +
  # plot 1st fitted gaussian curve
  stat_function(
    # multiply the 'mixing prop' (lambda) by density for every age -> adjusts the contribution of 1st gaussian to overall mixture
    fun = function(x) gmm_fit$lambda[1] * dnorm(x, gmm_fit$mu[1], gmm_fit$sigma[1]),
    color = "red",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  # plot 2nd fitted gaussian curve
  stat_function(
    # multiply the 'mixing prop' (lambda) by density for every age -> adjusts the contribution of 2nd gaussian to overall mixture
    fun = function(x) gmm_fit$lambda[2] * dnorm(x, gmm_fit$mu[2], gmm_fit$sigma[2]),
    color = "blue",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  # plot the sum of both gaussian curves
  geom_line(
    aes(y = gmm_fit$lambda[1] * dnorm(vitiligo_onset_BL, gmm_fit$mu[1], gmm_fit$sigma[1]) +
          gmm_fit$lambda[2] * dnorm(vitiligo_onset_BL, gmm_fit$mu[2], gmm_fit$sigma[2])),
    color = "purple",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Estimating early vs late age of onset",
    subtitle = "fitting bimodal gaussian distribution on VIGOR ages of onset",
    y = "density"
  )
```



```{r plot_bimodal_gmm_vit_age_onset_densityplot, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# init. coordinates of each peak
peak1_x <- gmm_fit$mu[1]
peak1_y <- gmm_fit$lambda[1] * dnorm(gmm_fit$mu[1], gmm_fit$mu[1], gmm_fit$sigma[1])
peak2_x <- gmm_fit$mu[2]
peak2_y <- gmm_fit$lambda[2] * dnorm(gmm_fit$mu[2], gmm_fit$mu[2], gmm_fit$sigma[2])

# plot the fitted bimodal gaussian model over our density plot
vit_age_onset_annotated_densityplot <- vit_age_onset_densityplot +
  # plot 1st fitted gaussian curve
  stat_function(
    # multiply the 'mixing prop' (lambda) by density for every age -> adjusts the contribution of 1st gaussian to overall mixture
    fun = function(x) gmm_fit$lambda[1] * dnorm(x, gmm_fit$mu[1], gmm_fit$sigma[1]),
    color = "red",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    x = gmm_fit$mu[1],
    y = 0,
    xend = gmm_fit$mu[1],
    yend = dnorm(gmm_fit$mu[1], gmm_fit$mu[1], gmm_fit$sigma[1]) * gmm_fit$lambda[1],
    color = "red",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  # plot 2nd fitted gaussian curve
  stat_function(
    # multiply the 'mixing prop' (lambda) by density for every age -> adjusts the contribution of 2nd gaussian to overall mixture
    fun = function(x) gmm_fit$lambda[2] * dnorm(x, gmm_fit$mu[2], gmm_fit$sigma[2]),
    color = "blue",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    x = gmm_fit$mu[2],
    y = 0,
    xend = gmm_fit$mu[2],
    yend = dnorm(gmm_fit$mu[2], gmm_fit$mu[2], gmm_fit$sigma[2]) * gmm_fit$lambda[2],
    color = "blue",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Estimating early vs late age of onset",
    subtitle = "fitting bimodal gaussian distribution on VIGOR ages of onset",
    y = "density",
    caption = NULL
  ) +
  annotate(
    geom = "label",
    x = c(peak1_x, peak2_x),
    y = c(peak1_y, peak2_y),
    label = str_c(c("First", "Second"), " Peak: ", c(round(peak1_x, 2), round(peak2_x, 2)), " years old", sep = ""),
    hjust = -0.05,
    vjust = -0.15,
    color = c("red", "blue")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15)))

vit_age_onset_annotated_densityplot
```

Now will use MAP estimation to assign each person to either "early onset" or "late onset"

```{r map_estimation_vit_age_onset, include=FALSE}
# init. posterior probabilities
posterior_probs <- gmm_fit$posterior

vit_age_onset_prediction_df <- vit_age_onset %>%
  filter(!is.na(vitiligo_onset_BL)) %>%
  mutate(
    # select the higher posterior for each person and label it early/late accordingly
    onset_classification = factor(apply(posterior_probs, 1, which.max), 
                              labels = c("early", "late")) %>% fct_relevel(c("early", "late")),
    # factorize and relevel
    plex = factor(plex) %>% fct_relevel(sort)
  )

vit_age_onset_prediction_df %>%
  select(
    patient_id, vit_status_exp, plex, vitiligo_onset_BL, onset_classification, everything()
  )
```

#### Logistic Regression


Use logistic regression to predict early vs. late-onset vitiligo in an affected individual based on their family type

```{r fit_log_reg_vit_age_onset, echo=FALSE}
# fit a logistic regression model
log_reg_fit <- glm(
  onset_classification ~ plex,
  data = vit_age_onset_prediction_df,
  # `binomial` specifies logistic regression
  family = binomial()
)

summary(log_reg_fit)
```

According to our fitted logistic regression model:

* The log odds of late onset for multiplex families is 0.3677
* The log odds of late onset increases by 0.1672 for simplex families compared to multiplex
* Neither the intercept nor `plexsimplex` are statistically significant
* Null deviance vs Residual deviance -- the small difference suggests this model doesn't explain much variation in the data


```{r include=FALSE}
vit_age_onset_prediction_df %>%
  # calculate predicted probabilities from fitted model
  mutate(predicted_prob = predict(log_reg_fit, type = "response")) %>%
  select(patient_id, vit_status_exp, plex, onset_classification, vitiligo_onset_BL, predicted_prob) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = vitiligo_onset_BL, y = predicted_prob)) +
  geom_jitter(
    aes(color = onset_classification),
    height = 0,
    width = 0.2,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) + 
  # facet_wrap(. ~ plex) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    # size = 2,
    alpha = 0.5,
    # color = "red"
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun.data = mean_cl_normal,
    geom = "errorbar",
    width = 0.2,
    color = "grey50"
  )
```

```{r}
# extract and analyze symptoms (multiple response format)
# this function will help parse the comma-separated symptom lists
parse_symptoms <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    # only include rows where people reported being sick
    filter(sickyesno_adhoc == "true") %>%
    # create a new col with symptoms as a list
    mutate(symptoms_list = str_split(symptoms_adhoc, ", ")) %>%
    # unnest the list to create one row per symptom
    unnest(symptoms_list) %>%
    # clean up symptom names
    mutate(symptoms_list = str_replace_all(symptoms_list, c("c\\(" = "", "\\)" = ""))) %>%
    mutate(symptoms_list = str_replace_all(symptoms_list, '"', "")) %>%
    # remove missing values
    filter(!is.na(symptoms_list), symptoms_list != "NULL", symptoms_list != "NA_character_", symptoms_list != "none") %>%
    # count symptoms
    count(symptoms_list) %>%
    # calculate percentage
    mutate(percentage = n /sum(df$sickyesno_adhoc == "true") * 100) %>%
    arrange(desc(n))
}

# apply the function to our data
symptom_counts <- parse_symptoms(adhoc_health)
print(symptom_counts)
```

### Hair Dye

#### Have you ever dyed your hair?

Is there a statistical association between coloring hair and having vitiligo?

```{r}
hair_change_bl <- env_exposures_nested_wide %>%
  unnest(cols = hair_change_BL, keep_empty = T) %>%
  mutate(hair_change_BL = factor(hair_change_BL, levels = c("true", "false"), labels = c(TRUE, FALSE)))
```


```{r}
# test for vitiligo status vs changing hair color
vit_vs_hairchange_chisq <- hair_change_bl %>%
  select(vit_status_exp, hair_change_BL) %>%
  table() %>%
  chisq.test()

# test for vitiligo status vs plex
vit_vs_plex_chisq <- hair_change_bl %>%
  select(vit_status_exp, plex) %>%
  table() %>%
  chisq.test()

# test for changing hair color vs plex
hairchange_vs_plex_chisq <- hair_change_bl %>%
  select(hair_change_BL, plex) %>%
  table() %>%
  chisq.test()

# do a fisher's exact test if we have small sample size (less than 5 for a category)
```

## DASH

```{r}
gc()
```


Steps to create a DASH spreadsheet for clinical team:

1. Retrieve data from Segment 31.1 in MDH
2. Download data and read it using the code in this section


```{r}
stop("Stop before DASH code")
```

DASH template:

* First Name
* Last Name
* Access Code: 99999**** (last 4 digits of phone number)
* Address
* Fourth Line: BLANK
* Name on Card: BLANK
* Data1: BLANK
* Data2: SPEEDTYPE (137880)
* Data3: BLANK
* Payment: BLANK
* Email





```{r}
# init. variables
ACCESS_CODE_PREFIX <- "99999"
SPEEDTYPE <- "137880"

DASH_COLS <- c(
  "name_first", "name_last", "access_code_or_ssn",
  "address1", "address2", "city", "state", "zip",
  "phone", "fourth_line", "name_on_card",
  "data1", "data2", "data3", "payment", "email"
)
```


```{r}
import_dir <- "~/U01_PROSPECTIVE_VITILIGO/data/mdh/exported_from_mdh"
import_file_base <- "vigor_prod_needs_compensation"
import_file <- str_subset(list.files(import_dir), import_file_base)
import_path <- file.path(import_dir, import_file)
# import_path


# import the CSV
dash_imp <- read_csv(import_path, show_col_types = F) %>%
  select(
    patient_id=ParticipantIdentifier,
    aou_complete=AOU_Complete,
    EnrollmentDate, CreatedDate,
    name_first=FirstName,
    name_last=LastName,
    email=EmailAddress,
    MobilePhone, ContactInfoPhone,
    address=ContactInfoAddress
  )
```




```{r}
dash_df <- dash_imp %>%
  mutate(
    # combine phone number fields and reformat them
    phone = coalesce(MobilePhone, ContactInfoPhone),
    phone = str_replace_all(phone, "[^\\d]*", "")
  ) %>%
  # extract address info 
  mutate(
    address = str_replace_all(address, "[\\\\{}]", "") %>%
      # add escape quotes to any present "null" values
      str_replace("null", "\"null\"") %>%
      # retrieve every unique item between escaped quotes
      str_extract_all('"([^"]*)"')
  ) %>%
  # selectively pull address elements and assign them names
  hoist(
    address,
    address1 = 2,
    address2 = 4,
    city = 6,
    state = 8,
    zip = 10
  ) %>%
  # reformat address info
  mutate(
    # remove extra escape characters and leave "null" values blank
    across(.cols = address1:zip,
           .fns = ~str_replace_all(.x, "\"|null", "")),
    # reformat zipcode to only contain first 5 digits
    zip = str_sub(zip, 1, 5)
  ) %>%
  # add additional DASH fields
  mutate(
    access_code_or_ssn = str_c(ACCESS_CODE_PREFIX, str_sub(phone, -4)),
    fourth_line = "",
    name_on_card = "",
    data1 = "",
    data2 = SPEEDTYPE,
    data3 = "",
    payment = ""
  ) %>%
  select(patient_id, all_of(DASH_COLS))
```



```{r eval=FALSE}
# export variables
export_path <- "~/U01_PROSPECTIVE_VITILIGO/data/foundry/surveys/dash/"
export_filename <- "vigor_prod_dash_template"
export_filetype <- ".xlsx"
update_date <- str_c(day(today()), str_to_upper(month.abb[month(today())]), year(today()))

# move existing files to "old_data/" directory
file_to_move <- str_subset(list.files(export_path), export_filename)
file.copy(from = str_c(export_path, file_to_move),
          to = str_c(export_path, "old_data/", file_to_move))
file.remove(from = str_c(export_path, file_to_move))


# write as an XLSX file
openxlsx::write.xlsx(
  x = dash_df %>% select(-patient_id),
  file = str_c(export_path,
               str_c(export_filename, update_date, sep = "_"),
               export_filetype)
)
```

```{r}
dash_prod_v2 <- dash_prod %>%
  mutate(
    # create new field to store participant info from surveys
    sv_field = case_when(str_detect(resultidentifier, "_BL") ~ str_replace(resultidentifier, "_BL", ""),
                         str_detect(resultidentifier, "ADDRESS") ~ "address")
  ) %>%
  select(patient_id:resultidentifier, sv_field, everything(),
         -c(surveydisplayname, surveyversion))
```


```{r}
dash_prod_v3 <- dash_prod_v2 %>%
  # remove cols that could uniquely identify different answers within a participant
  select(-c(surveyname:resultidentifier, recorded_date)) %>%
  # expand answers col to store important demographic info
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sv_field,
    values_from = answers
  ) %>%
  # flatten nested list-cols
  unnest_longer(c(email, first_name, last_name, phone, address)) %>%
  # remove records with duplicate patient IDs
  distinct(patient_id, .keep_all = T) %>%
  # format phone numbers to only consist of digits
  mutate(phone = str_extract_all(phone, "\\d") %>% pluck(1) %>% str_flatten() %>% str_sub(-10),
         .by = patient_id)
```


```{r}
# reformat and store address info
dash_prod_v4 <- dash_prod_v3 %>%
  mutate(
    # remove unnecessary escape characters
    address = str_replace_all(address, "[\\\\{}]", "") %>%
      # add escape quotes to any present "null" values
      str_replace("null", "\"null\"") %>%
      # retrieve every unique item between escaped quotes
      str_extract_all('"([^"]*)"')
  ) %>%
  # selectively pull address elements and assign them names
  hoist(
    address,
    address1 = 2,
    address2 = 4,
    city = 6,
    state = 8,
    zip = 10
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      # remove extra escape characters
      .cols = address1:zip,
      .fns = ~str_replace_all(.x, "\"", "")
    ),
    across(
      # replace any "null" values with NA
      .cols = address1:zip,
      .fns = ~str_replace_all(.x, "null", "")
    ),
    # reformat zipcode to only contain first 5 digits
    zip = str_sub(zip, 1, 5)
  ) %>%
  select(-address)
```

# TEST stats

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Data in two numeric vectors
women_weight <- c(38.9, 61.2, 73.3, 21.8, 63.4, 64.6, 48.4, 48.8, 48.5)
men_weight <- c(67.8, 60, 63.4, 76, 89.4, 73.3, 67.3, 61.3, 62.4) 

# Create a data frame
my_data <- tibble(group = factor(rep(c("Woman", "Man"), each = 9)),
                  weight = c(women_weight,  men_weight))


# compute summary stats by groups
my_data %>%
  summarize(
    count = n(),
    median = median(weight, na.rm = T),
    IQR = IQR(weight, na.rm = T),
    .by = group
  )
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
# 2. create a function to process participant data
surveys_clean %>%
  unnest(answers) %>%
  # convert dates to proper format
  mutate(
    enroll_day = as_date(enroll_date),
    months_from_baseline = as.numeric(difftime(recorded_date, enroll_day, units = "days")) / 30
  ) %>%
  # standardize responses
  mutate(
    standardize_response = case_when(
      # likert scales for stress
      answers %in% c("Never", "Almost Never", "Sometimes", "Fairly Often", "Very Often") ~
        factor(answers, levels = c("Never", "Almost Never", "Sometimes", "Fairly Often", "Very Often")) %>%
        as.numeric() - 1,
      # binary responses
      answers %in% c("true", "false") ~ as.numeric(answers == "true"),
      answers %in% c("Yes", "No") ~ as.numeric(answers == "Yes"),
      # numeric responses (leave as is)
      str_detect(answers, "^\\d+$") ~ as.numeric(answers),
      # default case
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  select(patient_id, enroll_day, recorded_date, months_from_baseline, answers, standardize_response)
```

```{r}
# columns to import to eShip
eship_cols <- c("name", "addressLine1", "addressLine2", "city", "state", "zip",
                "phone", "phoneCountry", "country", "email", "companyName")

# init. str extract patterns
fam_id_pat <- "(?<=VIGOR_)\\d+"
fam_pos_pat <- "\\d+(?=_v)|\\d+$"


fitbit_eship_df <- fitbit_needs_addy %>%
  mutate(
    # remove unnecessary escape characters
    ContactInfoAddress = str_replace_all(ContactInfoAddress, "[\\\\{}]", "") %>%
      # add escape quotes to any present "null" values
      str_replace("null", "\"null\"") %>%
      # retrieve every unique item between escaped quotes
      str_extract_all('"([^"]*)"')
  ) %>%
  # select(ParticipantIdentifier, ContactInfoAddress, ContactInfoAddressFormatted) %>%
  # selectively pull address elements and assign them names
  hoist(
    ContactInfoAddress,
    address1 = 2,
    address2 = 4,
    city = 6,
    state = 8,
    zip = 10
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      # remove extra escape characters
      .cols = address1:zip,
      .fns = ~ str_replace_all(.x, "\"", "")
    ),
    across(
      # replace any "null" values with NA
      .cols = address1:zip,
      .fns = ~ str_replace_all(.x, "null", "")
    ),
    across(
      # remove excess whitespace
      .cols = address1:zip,
      .fns = ~str_squish(.x)
    )
  ) %>%
  # create 1 col for names
  unite(FirstName, LastName, col = "name", sep = " ") %>%
  rename("addressLine1" = "address1",
         "addressLine2" = "address2",
         "companyName" = "ParticipantIdentifier") %>%
  mutate(
    # write states and country as 2 character codes
    state = str_to_title(state),
    state = case_when(
      # handle DC entries
      str_to_lower(state) == "dc" | str_detect(state, "(D|d)istrict") ~ "DC",
      # keep abbreviations that user already inputted
      str_length(state) == 2 ~ state.abb[match(str_to_upper(state), 
                                               state.abb,             # find position index of `state` match to `state.abb` vector
                                               nomatch = NA_character_)],
      # handle all other non-abbreviations
      .default = state.abb[match(state, 
                                 state.name,        # find position index of `state` match to `state.name` vector
                                 nomatch = NA_character_)]
    ), 
    country = case_when(str_to_title(state) %in% state.name | str_to_upper(state) %in% state.abb ~ "US",
                        .default = "CA")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # set phone country to be the same as the country (2 character code)
    phoneCountry = country,
    # addressLine2 = "",
    # combine MobilePhone + ContactInfoPhone and remove all non-digits from phone number
    phone = coalesce(MobilePhone, ContactInfoPhone) %>% str_replace_all("[^\\d]", ""),
    FamilyID = as.integer(str_extract(companyName, "(?<=VIGOR_)\\d+")),
    fam_pos = as.integer(str_extract(companyName, fam_pos_pat)),
    email = EmailAddress
  ) %>%
  select(any_of(eship_cols), FamilyID, fam_pos)


fitbit_eship_df
```

```{r}
### Check if columns are labelled correctly ###

# read in previous CSV of total invited VIGOR pts
full_cohort_imp_old <- read_csv(
  file = "/Users/tjacob/U01_PROSPECTIVE_VITILIGO/data/mdh/exported_from_mdh/old_data/vigor_prod_total_invited_2025_11_10.csv", 
  show_col_types = F
)

# specify expected column names and custom column names if rearrangement is needed
expected_mdh_cols <- colnames(full_cohort_imp_old)

# expected values for certain columns --> mislabelled cols will not have these values
correct_vals_gender <- c("F", "M", "O", NA)
correct_vals_studyendreason <- c("Deceased", "InvoluntaryWithdrawal", 
                                 "SoftDrop", "VoluntaryWithdawal", NA)




# function to detect whether a column is likely to be a 'Gender' column
is_column_correct <- function(x, correct_vals) {
  all(unique(na.omit(x)) %in% correct_vals)
}

# conditional relabeling based on column values
checked_imp <- full_cohort_imp %>%
  mutate(
    StudyEndReason_is_correct = is_column_correct(.data$StudyEndReason, correct_vals_studyendreason),
    StudyEndReason_is_gender = is_column_correct(.data$StudyEndReason, correct_vals_gender)
  )

# if StudyEndReason has correct expected values
if (checked_imp$StudyEndReason_is_correct[1]) {
  # keep imported DF as-is
  full_cohort_imp <- full_cohort_imp
  message("Keep DF exported from MDH as-is.")
  print(full_cohort_imp)
} else if (checked_imp$StudyEndReason_is_gender[1]) {
  # if StudyEndReason has values we'd expect for Gender col, read it in again with custom col order
  full_cohort_imp <- read_csv(
    file = str_c(inf_path, infile),
    show_col_types = F,
    col_names = mdh_cols_custom_order
  ) %>%
    slice_tail(n = -1)
  message("Read in MDH DF with custom column order.")
  print(full_cohort_imp)
} else {
  stop("MDH DF's columns are mislabelled and don't match the expected or custom column order we've defined. Requires manual re-labelling (`full_cohort_imp`).")
}
```

```{r}
  # extract just the numbers (account for entries with identical numbers but different format)
  mutate(phone = str_replace_all(MobilePhone, "[^0-9]", "")) %>%
  select(ParticipantIdentifier, MobilePhone, phone, everything()) %>%
  # filter for any duplicates among MDH pts --> retain if a dup belongs to a potential Fitbit pt
  filter(n() > 1, .by = MobilePhone) %>%
  semi_join(fitbit_to_inv, "ParticipantIdentifier")


if (nrow(dup_phones_to_inv) > 0) {
  print(dup_phones_to_inv %>% arrange(ParticipantIdentifier))
  stop("There is at least 1 non-unique `MobilePhone` among participants to ship to. Must fix this manually in MDH before proceeding.")
} else {print("No duplicate `MobilePhone` detected among the cohort to ship to. Continue!")}
```

Fix these manually in MDH!!



```{r eval=FALSE}
dup_phones_to_inv %>% 
  arrange(ParticipantIdentifier) %>%
  filter(str_detect(ParticipantIdentifier, "VIGOR_(21|1384|1419|414|342|748)_", negate = T))
```
